sub_graphs.title: EIP-3860: Initcode Gas Metering

nodes.label: Initcode Ready for Gas Calculation
nodes.description: Initcode passed size validation, ready for gas metering

nodes.label: Calculate Initcode Words
nodes.description: Compute ceil(len(initcode) / 32) to get word count

nodes.label: Compute Initcode Cost
nodes.description: Multiply words by INITCODE_WORD_COST (2 gas per word)

nodes.label: Initcode Cost Calculated
nodes.description: Total initcode gas cost determined

nodes.label: Add to Intrinsic Gas
nodes.description: Add initcode cost to transaction intrinsic gas requirement

nodes.label: Intrinsic Gas Updated
nodes.description: Transaction intrinsic gas includes initcode cost

nodes.label: Check Gas Limit Sufficient
nodes.description: Verify tx.gasLimit >= intrinsic gas (including initcode cost)

nodes.label: Insufficient Gas
nodes.description: Gas limit too low for intrinsic + initcode cost

sub_graphs.title: EIP-3860: DoS Mitigation via Initcode Limits
sub_graphs.description: Models how initcode limits mitigate jumpdest analysis DoS attacks

nodes.label: Large Initcode Submitted
nodes.description: Contract creation with large initcode received

nodes.label: Perform Jumpdest Analysis
nodes.description: Scan initcode to build valid JUMPDEST table

nodes.label: Analysis Cost Pre-EIP-3860
nodes.description: Before limits: ~1.3GB initcode possible, analysis very expensive

nodes.label: Analysis Cost Post-EIP-3860
nodes.description: After limits: max 49KB initcode, analysis bounded

nodes.label: DoS Vector Mitigated
nodes.description: Attack requiring ~80M additional gas, substantially more expensive

nodes.label: Charge Analysis Cost
nodes.description: Initcode metering ensures attacker pays for analysis overhead

external_entities.name: Malicious Actor
external_entities.description: Attacker attempting DoS via expensive jumpdest analysis

ambiguities.text: The EIP states size check is done 'before' lighter checks but doesn't enumerate all checks and their order
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume size check occurs after basic transaction format validation but before call depth and balance checks.

ambiguities.text: The term 'exceptional abort' for CREATE/CREATE2 is not precisely defined
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume exceptional abort behaves like out-of-gas: all remaining gas consumed, execution reverts, CREATE returns 0.

ambiguities.text: The EIP does not specify whether the limit applies to EOF container deployments differently
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume MAX_INITCODE_SIZE applies uniformly to all initcode regardless of format (legacy or EOF).

implicit_assumptions.description: All clients perform jumpdest analysis with similar computational cost per byte
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Clients with more expensive analysis could still be DoS vulnerable even with size limits

implicit_assumptions.description: Attackers cannot find ways to trigger expensive computation with initcode under the size limit
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: DoS vectors could still exist via algorithmic complexity attacks on smaller initcode

implicit_assumptions.description: 49152 bytes (2 * MAX_CODE_SIZE) is sufficient for legitimate contract deployments
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Legitimate use cases requiring larger initcode would be blocked

implicit_assumptions.description: Gas metering at 2 gas per 32-byte word adequately covers the computational cost of processing initcode
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Underpriced initcode processing could still allow resource exhaustion attacks
